name: Tetraethylene glycol
description: Tetraethylene glycol (CAS 112-60-7 ), commonly abbreviated as TEG, is a mid-chain polyethylene glycol marketed under the designation PEG-4 in cosmetic and personal care contexts. It functions as a hygroscopic solvent, humectant, and reactive intermediate across pharmaceutical, cosmetic, and polymer manufacturing applications. In personal care formulations, TEG acts as a humectant. It serves as a solvent carrier for active ingredients in creams, serums, and cleansing products, improving texture and moisture retention. Pharmaceutical manufacturers use it as a solvent and co-solvent. In topical and oral preparations, its low volatility supports stable, consistent dosing. In polymer chemistry, TEG serves as a reactive diol for cross-linking and curing polyurethane and epoxy systems. This contributes to controlled network density in coatings and adhesives. It also functions as a plasticizer and processing aid in specialty plastic formulations requiring flexible, low-migration performance. Tetraethylene glycol is supplied as a clear, low-viscosity liquid in drum and IBC quantities. Standard commercial grades include technical and high-purity specifications suited to industrial applications. Pharmaceutical and cosmetic supply chains typically require material meeting USP or Ph.
